name: Ixia-c (Open Traffic Generator)
what_it_is: Ixia-c is an API-driven, multi-container traffic generator that implements the Open Traffic Generator (OTG) standard, enabling programmatic generation and measurement of L2-7 network traffic for testing network devices. It runs as a distributed set of Docker containers controlled via a REST API or Python/Go SDKs.
components: keng-controller — orchestrates configuration, exposes HTTPS REST API on port 8443, accepts OTG JSON payloads
ixia-c-traffic-engine — per-port packet Tx/Rx engine, runs privileged with af_packet, listens on a configurable TCP port (default 5555/5556/5557)
keng-app-usage-reporter (aur) — optional telemetry/reporting sidecar, network_mode host
measurement: One-way latency per flow (minimum, maximum, average)
Packet capture with filtering, output as PCAP file or tcpdump redirection
configuration: REST API over HTTPS (port 8443) accepting OTG JSON payloads
Environment variables per traffic-engine container: OPT_LISTEN_PORT, ARG_IFACE_LIST, OPT_NO_HUGEPAGES, cpuset (CPU pinning)
modes: Rate specified as packets-per-second or percentage of line rate
constraints: Maximum 256 flows per port in the community edition
Requires minimum 2 x86_64 CPU cores and 7 GB RAM per deployment
Traffic engine containers must run privileged (privileged: true) to use af_packet
Community edition throughput is kbps–Gbps range; Tbps scale requires the commercial Keysight KENG variant
No hugepages by default (OPT_NO_HUGEPAGES=Yes); enabling hugepages requires host kernel configuration
Unsupported protocol headers (beyond the built-in 12) require external tooling such as Scapy to construct raw frames

docker_services.name: controller
docker_services.notes: Requires --accept-eula flag; uses host network mode

docker_services.name: traffic_engine_1
docker_services.notes: Privileged; af_packet interface binding; CPU pinned via cpuset

docker_services.name: traffic_engine_2
docker_services.notes: Privileged; af_packet interface binding; CPU pinned via cpuset

docker_services.name: traffic_engine_3
docker_services.notes: Present in three-arm topology only; same constraints as engine_1/2

docker_services.name: aur
docker_services.notes: Optional app usage reporter sidecar; host network mode

notable_absences: No built-in fault injection or packet loss/delay emulation — no netem or tc integration in provided compose files
No protocol state-machine (BGP, OSPF, IS-IS) in the community edition; emulated control-plane protocols require the commercial KENG license
No GUI — interaction is API-only (REST, snappi, gosnappi)
No native IPv6 management plane in compose files; controller API endpoint is IPv4 only in examples
